newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada should clean up royalty rules - Mobil.
newsitem.headline: Canada should clean up royalty rules - Mobil.

text.p: Canadian offshore oil and gas regulations are cumbersome and often unpredictable, Paul Hoenmans, Mobil Corp's executive vice-president said on Thursday.

"There's going to be more development in offshore Nova Scotia and what we want is the governments to set out what the offshore royalties schedule is before they (companies) start to explore," Hoenmans told Reuters after speaking at the Canadian Offshore Resources Exposition (CORE).
"We want that as a pre-known condition so that industry can then move in knowing what the regulations are," he said.
The Nova Scotia provincial government has no overall royalty regime, but negotiates fiscal terms on a project-by-project basis.
Canada's federal government already has a taxation regime in place, while Newfoundland implemented one earlier this year.
Also, Hoenmans criticized both the Nova Scotia and Newfoundland governments for lengthy regulatory reviews.
"It should take certainly not more than a year to conduct the public review process," Hoenmans said, noting that the process can take two or more years.
